challenges.name: sorted-set-rank-quiz
challenges.title: What does the sorted set really return?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the new Redis leaderboard: how equal scores are ordered, and why the top two learners saw an empty "Around you" box.

questions.question:
redis-cli on staging. u_1001 reached 90 points on Monday at 09:12, u_2040 reached 90 points two hours later, and the API called ZADD in that order:

> ZADD lb:week:2026-W44 90 u_1001
(integer) 1
> ZADD lb:week:2026-W44 90 u_2040
(integer) 1
> ZADD lb:week:2026-W44 120 u_0815
(integer) 1
> ZREVRANGE lb:week:2026-W44 0 -1 WITHSCORES
1) "u_0815"
2) "120"
3) "u_2040"
4) "90"
5) "u_1001"
6) "90"

Statement: "u_2040 is listed above u_1001 because, when scores are equal, Redis puts the member that was added most recently first."
questions.explanation: False. A sorted set stores only members and scores, not when a member was added. Members with equal scores are ordered by their bytes (lexicographically): ZRANGE lists u_1001 before u_2040, and ZREVRANGE reverses the whole order, so u_2040 comes first. Calling ZADD in the opposite order gives exactly the same output. If the product wants "first to reach the score ranks higher", that rule has to be encoded in the score itself (or the tie broken in PostgreSQL); insertion order will not do it. The misconception is that a sorted set behaves like a list that remembers arrival order.

questions.question:
GET /leaderboard/me builds the "Around you" box like this (ioredis):

const index = await redis.zrevrank("lb:all", learnerId);          // 0-based
const around = await redis.zrevrange("lb:all", index - 2, index + 2, "WITHSCORES");

The board has 4,812 members. Responses from production:

u_0815  index 0  -> around: []
u_2040  index 1  -> around: []
u_1001  index 2  -> around: 5 entries, ranks 1 to 5

Statement: "The box is empty for u_0815 because Redis reads the start index -2 as the second-to-last position of the set, which comes after the stop index 2."
questions.explanation: True. In ZRANGE and ZREVRANGE a negative index counts from the end: -1 is the last member, -2 the one before it. For u_0815 the request is 4810..2, and a start greater than the stop returns an empty list; for u_2040 it is 4811..3, also empty. Nothing fails loudly - the code just shows nothing for the two learners most likely to look. Clamp the start with Math.max(0, index - 2) before calling Redis. The misconception is that an index below zero is an error or is treated as 0.

challenges.name: leaderboard-top-n-and-rank
challenges.title: Leaderboard top N, rank and neighbours
challenges.description:
CodeDev's leaderboard page (GET /leaderboard?board=all|week and GET /leaderboard/me) moves from a slow PostgreSQL query to Redis sorted sets. PostgreSQL keeps every score event; Redis serves top N and ranks. Member = learnerId, score = points. Write four functions; the starter has the in-memory Redis model (zincrby, zscore, zrevrange, zrevrank, zcard, expire, ttl - same semantics as Redis, including negative indexes in zrevrange and lazy expiry on a fake clock).

Keys: lb:all is the all-time board and never expires. lb:week:<isoYear>-W<ww> is the board of one ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC to Sunday 23:59:59.999 UTC), with a two-digit week, for example lb:week:2026-W44. The ISO year is the year of the Thursday of that week: 2027-01-01 belongs to lb:week:2026-W53 and 2024-12-30 to lb:week:2025-W01.

weekKey(ts): the weekly key for a timestamp in milliseconds (UTC).

recordScore(redis, event, now): event = { learnerId, points, ts }, read from JSON, so check it at runtime. Valid: learnerId is a non-empty string, points an integer from 1 to 10000, ts an integer >= 0. Otherwise return false and change nothing. For a valid event, ZINCRBY lb:all, then the weekly board of ts (the event time, not now): a weekly board is kept until 7 days after its week ends, so retention end = Monday 00:00 UTC of the following week + 7 days. If retention end <= now, do not touch the weekly board (a late event must not bring an expired week back); otherwise ZINCRBY it and set its expiry with expire(key, Math.ceil((retention end - now) / 1000)). Return true.

topN(redis, key, n): the first n entries as { rank, learnerId, score }; [] when n < 1 or the board does not exist.

rankOf(redis, key, learnerId): null when the learner is not on the board (or the board does not exist); otherwise { rank, score, around }, where around lists the entries from two ranks above to two ranks below the learner, the learner included, with fewer entries at the top and bottom of the board.

Ranking rule: ranks are ordinal and 1-based and follow Redis order - higher score first, and for equal scores the order ZREVRANGE returns (the learner id that is greater in byte order comes first). Two learners never share a rank.

Input (stdin): { "ops": [...], "summary"?: true } where each op is clock (set now), score (recordScore), top, rank or ttl; times are ISO strings and a board is "all" or a time whose weekKey is used. Output: one line per op (score lines are replaced by a count with summary). Do not change the types, FakeClock, FakeRedis or the test runner.
hints: Which single command gives a learner's position on the board, and how do you turn that 0-based position into a window of up to five entries without passing Redis an index that means something else?

Look at four places: the Thursday of the event's week (it decides both the ISO year and the week number), the retention end compared with now before you touch a weekly key, the start index you pass to zrevrange for a learner near the top, and what zrevrange(key, 0, n - 1) returns when n is 0.

A similar board of four learners: u_9 70, u_4 50, u_8 50, u_2 10. zrevrank of u_9 is 0, so the window is indexes 0..2: 1. u_9 70 | 2. u_8 50 | 3. u_4 50 (equal scores: the greater id first). For u_2, zrevrank is 3 and the window is 1..3 because index 5 does not exist: 2. u_8 50 | 3. u_4 50 | 4. u_2 10. And for an event at 2025-12-30T10:00Z the week starts on Monday 2025-12-29, its Thursday is 2026-01-01, so the key is lb:week:2026-W01.

tests.name: All-time and weekly top N: equal scores keep Redis order and ranks are ordinal
Weekly keys: Sunday night and Monday morning, two-digit weeks and the TTL to retention end
The incident: the first, second and last learner get only neighbours that exist
ISO year at the turn of the year: 2020-W53, 2025-W01, 2026-W53 and 2027-W01
Late events, expired weeks, unknown learners and boards: null ranks and empty tops
